subject: mathematics
unit_title: Mathematical Habits, Place Value, and Rounding
title: Launch and diagnostic: making sense of unfamiliar problems
focus: making sense of unfamiliar problems
essential_question: How do we make sense of an unfamiliar problem, and how does place value help us round, add, and subtract within 1,000?
learning_objectives: Build an accurate mental model of making sense of unfamiliar problems using a concrete or visual representation before any symbol work.
Explain making sense of unfamiliar problems in the learner's own words and connect the representation to the notation.
Identify what would count as a correct and a mistaken use of making sense of unfamiliar problems.
success_criteria: The learner completes the task about making sense of unfamiliar problems.
The learner shows a model, calculation, or documented process rather than a bare answer.
The learner checks the work against the criteria and names one next step.
representations: base-ten blocks or paper place-value strips
materials: notebook, paper, or an accessible digital equivalent
pencil or an accessible response tool
the unit representation set: base-ten blocks or paper place-value strips; open number line; place-value chart
household or classroom objects may substitute for any named manipulative

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Ask for two or three items from earlier units that this lesson depends on. Do not grade this; use it to decide how much modeling making sense of unfamiliar problems will need.
Model making sense of unfamiliar problems with materials, a drawing, or a diagram before any symbols appear. Think aloud so the reasoning is audible, and name each step.
Connect the model of making sense of unfamiliar problems to the written notation, pointing at each part of the model as the matching symbol is written.
The learner tries one item involving making sense of unfamiliar problems while the adult or tutor watches and gives immediate, specific feedback on the reasoning, not just the answer.
The learner shows or explains the key idea of making sense of unfamiliar problems in one response and names the part that still feels unsteady.

student_activity: The learner works alongside the adult or tutor to build and label a model of making sense of unfamiliar problems, then writes the matching notation and explains how the two match.
formative_check: Show or explain the main idea of making sense of unfamiliar problems in one response, and name the part that still feels unsteady.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated target for making sense of unfamiliar problems: accuracy, the quality of the model or reasoning, and the revision. Accept any valid approach that meets the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

target_misconception.pattern: Subtracts the smaller digit from the larger in each column regardless of position.
target_misconception.diagnostic_probe: For 502 - 138, what happens in the ones place, and is that allowed?
target_misconception.repair_move: Model the minuend with base-ten materials and physically trade before recording the written step.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite for making sense of unfamiliar problems (reading and writing three-digit numbers), reteach with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.

Observed pattern: Subtracts the smaller digit from the larger in each column regardless of position. Ask: "For 502 - 138, what happens in the ones place, and is that allowed?" Then: Model the minuend with base-ten materials and physically trade before recording the written step.
Ask the learner to represent why the procedure for making sense of unfamiliar problems works before continuing to more items.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of making sense of unfamiliar problems, and do not start remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short spaced review rather than a longer session today.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before recording making sense of unfamiliar problems as mastered.

mastery_rule: One correct response cannot establish mastery of making sense of unfamiliar problems. Mastery requires accurate independent evidence plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, separated by time or by representation. Guided success is recorded as supported and is not weighted as independent evidence.
support: If the learner is not yet ready for making sense of unfamiliar problems, return to the smallest prerequisite, reteach it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. Prerequisites for this unit: reading and writing three-digit numbers; addition and subtraction within 100.
extension: Apply making sense of unfamiliar problems under a new constraint, compare two strategies and justify which is more efficient, or write an original problem and its worked solution. The learner may not complete another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional read-aloud; no voice input and no camera are required at any point.
Chunk directions to one action at a time and keep a worked example visible while the learner works.
Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, built, or manipulative-based responses whenever the standard allows it.
Offer reduced item counts, extended time, hidden or disabled timers, movement breaks, and a low-distraction setting.
Describe every representation in words so the lesson works with high-contrast print, screen readers, or no images at all.
Keep all diagrams static and describable; no animation, motion, or auto-advance is required to understand the mathematics.
Size interactive targets for touch and allow the whole task to be completed on a small screen or on paper.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language; an error is information about the next teaching move, never a judgment of the learner.
Allow a pause, break, or change of response mode at any time without recording it as a failure.
Do not require photographs, voice recordings, location, or any personal or family detail to complete a task.
Any task involving tools, heat, liquids, or moving about the home requires adult supervision and may be replaced with a paper alternative.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram or worked example illustrating making sense of unfamiliar problems.
media.fallback: Every representation in this lesson is fully described in words and can be built from paper, household objects, or a plain number line. No image, video, audio, or animation is required.

evidence_record.note: Mastery decisions are made from the recorded evidence type and adult-observed result. Storing the learner's raw answers is never required by this course.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw answers, private reflections, recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Notice one safe, optional example of making sense of unfamiliar problems in daily life and describe it. No purchase, account, photograph, or private disclosure is required.

answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated target for naming fractions from area models: accuracy, the quality of the model or reasoning, and the revision. Accept any valid approach that meets the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before recording naming fractions from area models as mastered.

mastery_rule: One correct response cannot establish mastery of naming fractions from area models. Mastery requires accurate independent evidence plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, separated by time or by representation. support: Do not reteach naming fractions from area models during this task. target_misconception.pattern: Partitions a shape into the right number of parts without equal areas and names them unit fractions.
target_misconception.diagnostic_probe: Do these four parts cover the same amount of space?
target_misconception.repair_move: Verify equal area by tiling or by overlaying the parts before naming the fraction.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Record that a prerequisite for perimeter, area, and shape classification in the completed design is not secure (area of rectangles). Do not reteach it now; this task must stay unsupported to count as independent evidence.

Record the pattern neutrally: Partitions a shape into the right number of parts without equal areas and names them unit fractions. Do NOT deliver the diagnostic probe or the repair move during this task. Both are scheduled for the day-17 reassessment.
Note that the recorded reasoning for perimeter, area, and shape classification in the completed design is thin. Ask for the reasoning only after the learner has finished and submitted the task.
After the task, confirm specifically that the reasoning for perimeter, area, and shape classification in the completed design was sound. Do not begin remediation.
Record the pattern for the day-17 reassessment. Do not interrupt the task to correct it.

Provide the access support. Extended time, reduced quantity, an alternate response mode, a break, or re-reading the directions never make the evidence guided and never change the standard being evidenced.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before recording perimeter, area, and shape classification in the completed design as mastered.

mastery_rule: One correct response cannot establish mastery of perimeter, area, and shape classification in the completed design. Mastery requires accurate independent evidence plus explanation on at least two separate occasions, separated by time or by representation. Guided success is recorded as supported and is not weighted as independent evidence.
support: Do not reteach perimeter, area, and shape classification in the completed design during this task. Access supports -- extended time, reduced quantity, alternate response mode, breaks, and re-reading the directions -- are always available and do not change the standard being evidenced. Record what you observe and act on it during the day-17 reassessment or the unit's prerequisite practice. Prerequisites for this unit: area of rectangles; addition within 1,000; unit fractions; shape names.
extension: Apply perimeter, area, and shape classification in the completed design under a new constraint, compare two strategies and justify which is more efficient, or write an original problem and its worked solution. The learner may not complete another learner's graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional read-aloud; no voice input and no camera are required at any point.
Chunk directions to one action at a time and keep a worked example visible while the learner works.
Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, built, or manipulative-based responses whenever the standard allows it.
Offer reduced item counts, extended time, hidden or disabled timers, movement breaks, and a low-distraction setting.
Describe every representation in words so the lesson works with high-contrast print, screen readers, or no images at all.
Keep all diagrams static and describable; no animation, motion, or auto-advance is required to understand the mathematics.
Size interactive targets for touch and allow the whole task to be completed on a small screen or on paper.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language; an error is information about the next teaching move, never a judgment of the learner.
Allow a pause, break, or change of response mode at any time without recording it as a failure.
Do not require photographs, voice recordings, location, or any personal or family detail to complete a task.
Any task involving tools, heat, liquids, or moving about the home requires adult supervision and may be replaced with a paper alternative.

media.suggestion: Optional blank recording template only -- grid paper, a blank number line, or a blank table. No worked example, no diagram of perimeter, area, and shape classification in the completed design, and no model of the method is provided during this task.
media.fallback: Every representation in this lesson is fully described in words and can be built from paper, household objects, or a plain number line. No image, video, audio, or animation is required.

evidence_record.note: Mastery decisions are made from the recorded evidence type and adult-observed result. Storing the learner's raw answers is never required by this course.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw answers, private reflections, recordings, or diagnosis language.
home_connection: Notice one safe, optional example of perimeter, area, and shape classification in the completed design in daily life and describe it. No purchase, account, photograph, or private disclosure is required.
